paragraphs.text: [Meizhan](yancha:meizhan) is a Fujian cultivar that came from Anxi and is also made as [Wuyi rock tea](yancha:definition). It is less known than Rougui and Shui Xian and sits outside the four famous bushes of Wuyi. This leaf, from 1990, grew in the Wuyi Mountains, the only area whose tea may carry the rock tea name, where the bushes root among crevices, ledges and terraces in cliff country. It was twisted into long thin strips and finished over charcoal in several rounds, a [roast](yancha:making) that dries the leaf so it keeps.

Rock tea meant for [keeping](yancha:ageing) is the medium to full roast kind, since the heavier the roast, the longer it is said to stay good. Over thirty-six years, damp is the main risk. Tea that takes on moisture can go green again, fǎn qīng, the main fault of stored rock tea, so a tea kept this long has to stay sealed, dry and cool, and be checked now and then.

brewing.text: Wuyi tea is usually brewed gongfu style with water at or near the boil, about 95 to 100°C, and about 5 to 8 grams of leaf in a 100 to 120 ml gaiwan, a third to a half full. A quick rinse, poured off at once, is common. Steeps start short, about 5 to 20 seconds, and grow a few seconds longer each round, and good rock tea gives seven steeps or more. In a larger pot, use about 2 to 5 grams for 250 to 350 ml and steep two to three minutes.

notice.text: A smoother, thicker liquor with less sharpness, the roast softened and the high aroma faded.
